headline: The White House cleared vetted private firms to launch cyberattacks on foreign criminals, a first for US policy, as Germany moved to arm its spy agencies with hacking powers.

emerging_trends.text: Washington and Berlin both moved this week to legitimize state-blessed offensive hacking, the White House deputizing private firms and Germany empowering its intelligence services.
Public proof-of-concept code keeps compressing the gap to exploitation, with attackers hitting Microsoft SharePoint and Adobe Commerce within hours of the technical details going out.
emerging_trends.topic_title: SharePoint and Adobe Commerce Exploited After Disclosure

emerging_trends.text: Iran-linked crews kept probing US water utilities, reaching Minnesota and at least seven states, while attribution curdled into a political fight over who to blame.

topics.title: Governments Sanction Offensive Hacking
topics.latest_developments: President Trump signed a National Security Presidential Memorandum on August 12 directing the National Coordination Center to let vetted private companies apply to run offensive operations against foreign cybercrime groups, the first time Washington has authorized the private sector to conduct cyberattacks, while Germany's cabinet approved a parallel overhaul empowering its spy agencies to hack foreign systems and sabotage adversaries' supply chains.
topics.summary: The US memo places private hack-back operations under government control and oversight, with contracts that may require a $1 million bond forfeited for noncompliance; Germany's bill marks the biggest rewrite of its postwar intelligence law, adding authority to feed false information to extremists inside the country.

sources.title: Private security firms will soon be allowed to hack overseas cybercriminals
White House taps security firms for offensive hack-back operations
White House Mobilizes Security Firms for Operations Against Foreign Cybercrime Gangs
Germany moves to give spy agencies hacking and sabotage powers

topics.title: VMware vCenter Global Exploitation Campaign
topics.latest_developments: Dark Reading reports the exploitation of directory-traversal flaw CVE-2026-59310 in VMware vCenter's Syslog Server has grown into a global campaign, and warns that applying Broadcom's patch may not fully evict attackers who already deployed a reverse SSH tool for persistence.
topics.summary: The critical bug lets remote attackers execute arbitrary code on vCenter servers; administrators should patch immediately and hunt for reverse SSH implants and other persistence rather than assume the update alone remediates the intrusion.

sources.title: Global Threat Campaign Hits Critical VMware vCenter Flaw
Critical VMware vCenter RCE flaw exploited for reverse SSH access
Critical VMware vCenter Vulnerability in Attackers' Crosshairs

topics.title: SharePoint and Adobe Commerce Exploited After Disclosure
topics.latest_developments: Threat actors began actively exploiting Microsoft SharePoint authentication-bypass flaw CVE-2026-55040 after Rapid7 published proof-of-concept code, and separate attackers hit Adobe Commerce and Magento flaw CVE-2026-71362 within hours of Adobe releasing its fix.
topics.summary: CVE-2026-55040, rated 9.1, lets attackers impersonate users to disclose and modify SharePoint files and shipped in Microsoft's July 2026 Patch Tuesday; the Adobe Commerce bug enables customer-account hijacking, and both demand urgent patching now that working exploits circulate.

sources.title: Attackers Exploit SharePoint Authentication Bypass After Public PoC Release
Attackers exploit critical SharePoint flaw after PoC goes public (CVE-2026-55040)
Adobe Commerce Bug Targeted Immediately After Disclosure

topics.title: LegacyHive Windows Zero-Day Patched
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft released patches for a Windows zero-day dubbed LegacyHive, disclosed after the July 2026 Patch Tuesday, a distinct flaw from the Lazarus-linked bug and the ShieldBreak privilege-escalation exploit already circulating.
topics.summary: LegacyHive adds to a crowded month of exploited Windows flaws; organizations should apply the out-of-band fix and prioritize hosts exposed to the earlier SYSTEM-level exploits.

sources.title: Microsoft patches LegacyHive Windows zero-day vulnerability

topics.title: Iran Water Attacks Reach Minnesota
topics.latest_developments: Bruce Schneier reports the Iran-linked campaign against US water systems reached Minnesota and now spans at least seven states, while President Trump publicly rejected the Iran attribution and blamed Minnesota's government, calling the state grossly incompetent.
topics.summary: Investigators tie the intrusions to Iran targeting internet-exposed control systems at water utilities; attribution remains preliminary and no physical damage has surfaced, but the spread underscores exposure of small water and wastewater operators.

sources.title: Iran Cyberattacks Against Minnesota Water Systems

topics.title: Akira Disables EDR via Safe Mode
topics.latest_developments: BleepingComputer detailed an Akira ransomware affiliate that rebooted a compromised machine into Safe Mode with Networking to knock out its endpoint detection and response tool, then stole data but failed to encrypt files.
topics.summary: The Safe Mode trick strips security agents that do not load in the minimal environment, a durable evasion technique defenders can blunt by restricting reboots and enforcing EDR tamper protection and Safe Mode boot controls.

sources.title: Akira hackers disable EDR with Safe Mode, steal data but fail to encrypt

business_politics.title: U.S. 30-Year Bonds Sell at Highest Yield Since 2001
business_politics.latest_developments: The Treasury's August 13 sale of 30-year bonds cleared at the highest borrowing cost since 2001 as long-dated yields climbed on debt and inflation worries.
business_politics.summary: The U.S. Treasury sold 30-year bonds at yields last seen in 2001, with buyers demanding more to hold long-dated federal debt amid mounting public borrowing and persistently high inflation, a warning sign on the government's fiscal path. The same day the S&P 500 closed at a record high after a report of moderated wholesale inflation eased fears of a Federal Reserve rate move.

around_town.title: Pennsylvania Keeps Childhood Vaccine Schedule
around_town.latest_developments: Pennsylvania health officials said August 13 the state will keep its existing childhood immunization schedule despite President Trump's new executive order.
around_town.summary: The Pennsylvania Department of Health will follow its existing childhood vaccine schedule, state officials said, declining to adopt President Trump's executive order that cuts the number of advised shots and decouples some combination vaccines. "We will follow the facts," officials said.
